comment: What a position IS, when nothing else can tell.
Rapport works this out in three steps, and this file is the first of them:
1. this file, by position id -- somebody looked and said
2. the pack's own tags        -- 98.8% of positions on the reference install
3. the position's NAME        -- takes that to 99.2%
So this is deliberately SMALL. A full hand-built inventory would be over a
thousand entries here, 99% of them a second copy of data that ships with the
pack and goes stale the moment that pack updates. The tags stay current; a
You do not have to find the entries yourself. On every launch Rapport logs
every position whose act it cannot read, already formatted for pasting in --
and that list comes from the classifier that actually runs, so it can never
disagree with the rules being applied.
Values: oral | pleasure | kiss | climax | none
none means 'this is not a sexual act', which stops a face being applied at
all -- use it for utility and transition positions.
This also OVERRULES the tags, so it is the place to correct an author who
tagged something wrongly, not only to fill a silence.
